analysis:
## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** Advanced Medical Technology Association (AdvaMed), Diagnostic Payment Work Group (DPWG); signed by Zoe Guengerich, Senior Director, Payment & Healthcare Delivery Policy
- **Stakeholder type:** Professional Association (representing medical device, diagnostic products, and health IT manufacturers)
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** AdvaMed represents world's leading innovators and manufacturers of medical devices, diagnostic products, digital health technologies, and health information systems, including hundreds of small companies; responded specifically on behalf of clinical laboratory and diagnostic testing members.

---

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

AdvaMed's Diagnostic Payment Work Group responds exclusively to the RFI questions on laboratory testing prior authorization, identifying six systemic problems: (1) MA organizations improperly preventing laboratories from initiating PA requests despite existing CMS regulations; (2) inconsistent coverage criteria through LBMs that don't align with Medicare FFS LCD/NCD policy; (3) denial of services even when complete information is provided on TRFs; (4) post-specimen-collection PA denials based on misuse of the Medicare date-of-service policy; (5) inadequate transparency and accountability for LBM-delegated PA decisions; and (6) AI tools trained on non-CMS criteria amplifying inappropriate denials. AdvaMed urges CMS to codify laboratory PA rights, require TRF acceptance as valid documentation, clarify date-of-service rules, mandate LBM transparency reporting, and ensure AI oversight.

---

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** GENERAL (RFI on laboratory testing PA — corresponds to S66-S82 domain)
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** 42 C.F.R. § 422.566(c)(1)(ii) (coverage determinations, labs as providers); 42 C.F.R. § 422.138(b) (MA coverage nondiscrimination); 42 CFR 414.510(a) (Part B laboratory date of service policy); CMS Medicare Managed Care Manual, ch. 4, sec. 10.16; LCD L38779 (MRD Testing for Cancer); billing article A58376; MolDX article 14A59741; Humana Liquid Biopsy Medical Coverage Policy HUM-1151-001; NCD 90.2 (Liquid Biopsy); 91 Fed. Reg. 19890 (April 14, 2026)
- **Standards referenced:** NCDs, LCDs, billing articles, DEX™ Diagnostics Exchange Registry (Palmetto GBA MolDX), TRFs (Test Requisition Forms), ICD-10 coding, NPI numbers; no FHIR or NCPDP standards specifically addressed

---

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: Laboratories' Right to Initiate Prior Authorization**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Clarify / Modify (enforce existing regulation)
- **Rationale:** Some MAOs do not permit laboratories to submit PA requests despite 42 C.F.R. § 422.566 establishing labs as providers eligible to request coverage determinations. This creates procedural denials unrelated to medical necessity and forces patients and ordering providers to navigate inappropriate barriers.
- **Specific request:** CMS should include a new enforcement requirement ensuring MAO compliance with 42 C.F.R. § 422.566; clarify that labs may always initiate PA; establish mechanisms for providers to report non-compliance systemically rather than claim-by-claim.

**Topic 2: Inconsistent MA Coverage Criteria — LCDs, NCDs, and LBMs**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Oppose (current LBM practices) / Modify
- **Rationale:** MAOs contract with LBMs who use proprietary criteria inconsistent with Medicare FFS coverage, impose duplicative documentation demands, and are not incentivized to resolve disputes with laboratories. Billing articles and DEX™ registry resources that supplement LCDs are not being required for consideration, creating coverage disparities between MA and traditional Medicare.
- **Specific request:** Require MAOs to consider billing articles and databases (e.g., DEX™) when making coverage decisions; require any MA coverage policy distinct from an LCD or NCD to be publicly posted and subject to public comment before adoption; require UM committees to explicitly review criteria used by third-party entities like LBMs; require plans to report their use of third-party entities and their denial/appeal metrics.

**Topic 3: Test Requisition Forms (TRFs) as Valid Medical Documentation**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Support (codification)
- **Rationale:** CMS contractors (MolDX) have already clarified TRFs may establish medical necessity when complete, but MAOs continue denying NCD- and LCD-covered services despite complete TRF information. Codifying TRF acceptance would align MA with Medicare FFS and reduce duplicative documentation requests.
- **Specific request:** CMS should explicitly codify in MA regulations that TRFs are valid forms of medical documentation; adopt MolDX clarification across MA and commercial payers.

**Topic 4: Post-Specimen-Collection PA Denials / Date of Service Misuse**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Oppose (current practice) / Clarify
- **Rationale:** Some MA plans apply the Medicare Part B date-of-service policy (42 CFR 414.510(a)) to deny PA requests after specimen collection, even though the laboratory may not receive the specimen for up to 48 hours. This is inconsistent with 42 C.F.R. § 422.138(b).
- **Specific request:** CMS should clarify that MA plans must recognize the date of performance (when lab receives specimen) as the relevant date of service for PA purposes; clarify that denied claims are always appealable on medical necessity grounds regardless of PA outcome.

**Topic 5: Appeals Process Deficiencies**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** MA appeals window is 65 days vs. 120 days for Medicare FFS; collecting documentation from ordering providers can take up to 90 days; some plans only allow patients (not providers) to appeal; some denials are not escalated to third-party review because they are characterized as administrative (not medical necessity) denials; plans sometimes fail to reverse denials even after successful appeals.
- **Specific request:** Extend MA Level 1 appeal deadline to align with Medicare FFS (120 days); ensure all denied claims are appealable on medical necessity grounds; mandate clear escalation and dispute resolution processes for providers.

**Topic 6: Laboratory Benefit Managers (LBMs) — Transparency and Accountability**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify / Oppose (current accountability gap)
- **Rationale:** LBMs operate with minimal accountability, providing vague denial rationales, applying policies inconsistently, and redirecting disputes between MAOs and delegated entities without resolution.
- **Specific request:** Require MAOs to report annually: share of PA requests delegated to each third-party entity, share denied, share timely appealed, and share overturned on appeal; CMS should compile and publicly report this data.

**Topic 7: AI in Prior Authorization**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Conditional Support / Concern
- **Rationale:** AI tools could reduce manual documentation review and speed determinations, but documented cases show MA plans training AI on inconsistent Medicare guideline interpretations, leading to inappropriate PA denials that get systematically amplified at scale.
- **Specific request:** Require AI tools to be trained on official Medicare guidelines (NCDs, LCDs, billing articles); require MAOs to submit information on their use of AI in coverage decision-making for public reporting; consider excluding sufficiently complex disease groups/patient populations/procedures from AI utilization in coverage determinations.

**Topic 8: Consider Eliminating PA for NCD/LCD-Covered Services**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Recommend
- **Rationale:** Given the high overturn rate on appeals (80.7% in 2024) and the time-sensitive nature of diagnostic testing, requiring prior authorization for services explicitly covered under NCDs or LCDs may not be appropriate.
- **Specific request:** CMS should consider whether MAOs should require PA at all where defined NCD or LCD coverage policy exists.

---

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

This comment responds exclusively to the RFI on laboratory testing (S66-S82 domain), not to specific numbered solicitations in the main proposed rule. AdvaMed explicitly limits its response to laboratory testing questions posed in the RFI.

- **RFI (Lab PA impact on patient care/provider burden):** PA policies preventing labs from initiating requests, LBM inconsistency, TRF denials, and DOS misuse cause delays in time-sensitive oncology and precision medicine testing; 80.7% appeal overturn rate demonstrates systemic initial denial problems.
- **RFI (TRFs as valid documentation):** Codifying TRF acceptance would align MA with Medicare FFS, reduce duplicative documentation, and reduce inappropriate denials; CMS contractors already recognize TRFs as sufficient.
- **RFI (Frequency of post-collection PA denials):** DOS policy misuse allows MA plans to deny PA on procedural grounds after specimen collection; date of performance (not collection) should govern.
- **RFI (LBM impact):** LBMs impose extra criteria inconsistent with Medicare coverage rules; lack clear accountability; UM committees should be required to review LBM-used criteria.
- **RFI (Process improvement opportunities):** Eliminate PA for NCD/LCD-covered services; codify TRF acceptance; require that all denials are appealable on medical necessity grounds; mandate escalation/dispute resolution pathways.
- **RFI (AI automation impact):** AI could improve timeliness but risks amplifying coverage misinterpretations if trained on non-authoritative criteria; requires CMS oversight, mandatory reporting, and validation.
- **RFI (Issues technology isn't addressing):** Lack of clear escalation/dispute resolution pathways; fundamental misalignment between MA and Medicare FFS coverage policies that technology cannot fix without regulatory enforcement.
- **RFI (Workforce and retention):** Administrative burdens from repeated denials and appeals divert clinical/lab staff from patient care, contributing to burnout and reduced participation in MA networks.

---

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Include a new requirement ensuring MAO compliance with 42 C.F.R. § 422.566 (lab PA initiation rights); establish systemic (not claim-by-claim) reporting mechanisms.
2. Require MAOs to consider LCD billing articles and databases (e.g., DEX™ registry) when making coverage decisions.
3. Require any MA coverage policy distinct from an LCD or NCD to be publicly posted and subject to public comment before adoption.
4. Require UM committees to explicitly review criteria used by third-party entities (e.g., LBMs), not just MAO-developed criteria.
5. Explicitly codify in MA regulations that TRFs are valid medical documentation; adopt MolDX clarification across MA and commercial payers.
6. Clarify that MA plans must use date of performance (not date of specimen collection) as the relevant date of service for lab PA purposes.
7. Clarify that all denied claims are always appealable on medical necessity grounds, regardless of PA outcome.
8. Extend MA Level 1 appeal deadline to align with Medicare FFS (120 days).
9. Mandate clear escalation and dispute resolution processes for providers contending MA plans are not following rules.
10. Require MAOs to report annually on PA requests delegated to third-party entities (LBMs), share denied, share appealed, share overturned; CMS to compile and publish.
11. Require AI tools used in PA to be trained on official Medicare guidelines (NCDs, LCDs, billing articles); require public reporting of AI use in coverage decisions; consider excluding complex disease groups from AI-based coverage determinations.
12. Consider whether MAOs should require PA at all where defined NCD or LCD coverage policy exists.
13. Require collection and public reporting of MA claim denial data disaggregated by service type, with comparison to Medicare FFS.

---

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** MA plans and LBMs systematically using procedural/administrative grounds (not medical necessity) to deny laboratory PA; high initial denial rates (80.7% overturn on appeal in 2024); 65-day MA appeal window too short when acquiring provider records takes up to 90 days; AI tools trained on incorrect criteria amplifying inappropriate denials at scale.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** Delays in time-sensitive oncology and precision medicine diagnostic testing; patients losing access to medically necessary services on technicalities; laboratories unable to meaningfully appeal administrative denials; workforce burnout from repetitive denial/appeal cycles.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** Labs are ancillary providers unable to acquire ordering provider documentation within short appeal windows; LBMs create accountability gaps between MAO and delegated entity; no systemic dispute resolution pathway short of individual claim appeals.

---

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** 53 million MA PA determinations in 2024 (KFF, Jan 28, 2026); 11.5% of denied PA requests appealed in 2024; 80.7% of those appeals partially or fully overturned (KFF).
- **Studies or research referenced:** KFF report (Biniek et al., Jan. 28, 2026) on MA PA determinations; CMS RFI (91 Fed. Reg. 19890) acknowledging DOS policy misuse and TRF acceptance gaps.
- **Examples provided:** Humana Liquid Biopsy Medical Coverage Policy (HUM-1151-001) improperly applying LCD criteria to an NCD-covered service; LCD L38779 (MRD Testing for Cancer) with complex multi-criteria billing articles; colorectal cancer screening denials based on medical records review when medical necessity can be determined from demographic/ICD-10 data.

---

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** Clinical and diagnostic testing laboratories, MA beneficiaries, ordering physicians, MAOs, LBMs, AdvaMed members (diagnostic product manufacturers).
- **Economic implications:** Uncompensated care from procedural denials; administrative burden from duplicative appeals and documentation gathering; workforce costs from PA-related staff time diversion.
- **Technical feasibility:** AdvaMed's primary recommendations (LBM reporting, TRF codification, DOS clarification) are regulatory rather than technical and feasible through existing rulemaking mechanisms; AI oversight recommendations require new reporting infrastructure.
- **Patient care impact:** Delays in time-sensitive oncology/precision medicine diagnostics directly affect treatment decisions and patient outcomes; high overturn rates suggest many denied services are medically necessary.

---

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Concerned / Opposed (to current MA PA practices)
- **Tone:** Professional, Technical, Critical (of current MA/LBM practices)
- **Priority level:** High

---

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "Technology alone cannot resolve the fundamental misalignment between MA coverage policies and Medicare FFS rules without stronger CMS enforcement and accountability mechanisms." — Context: Responding to RFI question on issues technology is not currently addressing.

2. "The high overturn rate strongly suggests that many initial denials lack merit and that systematic improvements to the prior authorization process—not merely the appeals process—are warranted." — Context: Citing 80.7% appeal overturn rate to argue for structural PA reform, not just appeals reform.

3. "There is no disincentive for plans to continue this practice of high denials and no recourse for laboratories and other third-party providers." — Context: Describing how the 65-day MA appeal window combined with 90-day documentation retrieval times effectively insulates plans from accountability.

4. "Improperly implemented AI tools risk amplifying existing coverage misinterpretations and denial patterns if not subject to CMS oversight and validation." — Context: Warning about AI used in PA trained on inconsistent MA/Medicare guidelines.

---

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **PROVIDER-BURDEN** — Administrative burdens from PA denials, duplicative documentation requests, inadequate appeals windows, and LBM redirect loops directly burden clinical laboratory staff and divert time from patient care.
- [x] **TRANSPARENCY** — Recommends public posting of MA-developed coverage policies before adoption; requires LBM denial/appeal data reporting; supports public reporting of AI use in coverage decisions.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** — Core concern: delays in time-sensitive oncology/precision medicine testing affect treatment decisions; post-collection denials interrupt established clinical workflows.
- [x] **REGULATORY-AUTHORITY** — Calls on CMS to enforce existing 42 C.F.R. § 422.566 and § 422.138(b); argues some current MA practices violate existing law.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** — Laboratory PA workflows inherently sequential (specimen collection → shipment → testing); existing MA date-of-service policy misapplication breaks this workflow.
- [x] **VENDOR-ECOSYSTEM** — LBMs as third-party contracted entities operating with proprietary criteria inconsistent with CMS rules represent a systemic accountability gap.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** — AI tools in PA could improve timeliness but risk amplifying biases if not trained on authoritative CMS guidance; requires regulatory safeguards.
